summary: Stephen Prothero is a religious studies scholar who studied at Yale University and Jonathan Edwards College (B.A.) and earned his M.A. and Ph.D. under William R. Hutchison at Harvard. He held a professorship at Boston University from around 1996.

Stephen R. Bokenkamp, a scholar of sinology and religious studies, studied at the University of California, Berkeley (1976–1986). He served at Indiana University Bloomington (~1989–2007) and Arizona State University (~2007), and was a visiting fellow at ANU (1999).
Stephen Suen is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2009).

Stephen Wootton Bushell was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Guy's Hospital Medical School and the University of London (MD), serving as house surgeon at Guy's Hospital (1866) and resident medical officer at Bethlem Royal Hospital (1867).

Steve Odin is a scholar of philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Stony Brook University under Robert Cummings Neville, David A. Dilworth, Don Ihde, and Edward S. Casey, and became Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hawaiʻi in 1982.

Steven Collins (1950–2018) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his D.Phil. at Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Michael Carrithers, later holding posts at the universities of Bristol, Indiana, and Chicago, among other institutions.

Steven Edward Lindquist is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Texas at Austin under Patrick Olivelle, also studying with traditional teachers. He held a post at Concordia University.

Steven Heine is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Pennsylvania, Temple University, and under Shudo Ishii. He held posts at Villanova, La Salle, Pennsylvania State University, and Florida International University.

Steven Lukes is a scholar of philosophy and other fields who studied at Oxford under E. E. Evans-Pritchard. He held faculty posts at Balliol College, Oxford, the University of Florence, European University Institute, LSE, and New York University.

Steven Weinberger is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Amherst College and the University of Virginia, completing his Ph.D. under Jeffrey Hopkins, and held an affiliation with the University of Virginia (attested 2006).
Stewart McFarlane is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and sinology who held posts in the Department of Religious Studies at Lancaster University (attested 1991, 2001).

Sthaneshwar Timalsina is an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. He held faculty posts at Nepal Sanskrit University, San Diego State University, and Stony Brook University.

Stig Wikander (1908–1983) was an Indology, Iranian/Central Asian, and religious studies scholar who studied at Uppsala, Paris, Copenhagen, and Berlin, completing his doctorate under H. S. Nyberg. He held posts at Lund University and Uppsala University.
Stuart H. Blackburn is an Indologist who studied at Wesleyan University (~1965–1969) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1973–1980). He held a post at SOAS University of London (~1993–2011).

Stuart Piggott (1910–1996) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at University College London and the UCL Institute of Archaeology (~1935–1936), later holding a post at the University of Edinburgh (~1946–1977).
Stuart Ray Sarbacker is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin–Madison in 2001 under the supervision of David M. Knipe.

Subhadradis Diskul (1923–2003) was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at Chulalongkorn, École du Louvre under Philippe Stern, and the University of London. He served at the Bangkok National Museum, as Silpakorn University's rector, and as SPAFA director.

Subhash Kak is an Indologist and engineer who studied at NIT Srinagar and IIT Delhi under P. V. Indiresan. He held major professorships at Louisiana State University (1979) and Oklahoma State University (2007).

Subrata K. Mitra is a scholar of history and archaeology who studied at Utkal University, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Rochester. He held posts at the universities of Hull, California (Berkeley), Heidelberg, and the National University of Singapore.

Sucheng Chan is a historian who studied at Swarthmore College, the University of Hawaiʻi, and the University of California, Berkeley. She served as a professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara from around 1984 to 2005.
